seeds.title: Remove the MVTec cosine-reconstruction objective
seeds.description: Delete the repository's only cosine-distance implementation. The industrial-image method is reported as training its decoder with a three-scale cosine reconstruction loss, and the MVTec conclusions in Tables 2 and 4 depend on that objective. After this deletion there is no implementation of the stated loss anywhere in the repository, so the reported industrial reconstruction pipeline cannot be produced rather than merely producing a wrong substitute.
seeds.expected_reasoning: A careful auditor first identifies Eq. (9) in the appendix as the MVTec reconstruction objective, then searches the release for cosine similarity. The only match implementing the loss is cosine_similarity in utils/utils.py. The patch removes the entire function and leaves no call-equivalent implementation, while the tabular MSE objective remains. Thus no code backs the paper's industrial cosine-reconstruction experiment; because no replacement computation remains, this is MISS rather than BUG.
seeds.paper_anchor: We apply the cosine similarity loss to replace the original Lrec

seeds.title: Remove the industrial-image contraction-flow model
seeds.description: Delete denoise_net.py, the only visual patch-flow implementation: it contains the 768-channel DenoiseFlow, its flow assemblies, inversion path, and sampling path used for spatial feature maps. The tabular vector flow remains, but no code remains for applying the contraction flow to MVTec multi-layer patch embeddings, so the paper's industrial-image pipeline and its classification/localization results have no implementation.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The appendix says that fused encoder feature maps are passed through a contraction flow before decoding and patch-level likelihood scoring. A repository search shows that denoise_net.py alone implements a B-by-N-by-C flow with the 768-channel default corresponding to the fused image representation; denet.py only implements the released tabular B-by-C model. Deleting the visual flow file removes the complete relevant forward/inverse mechanism and leaves no runnable code path for that reported experiment. Nothing executes in its place, satisfying MISS.
seeds.paper_anchor: Based on this baseline framework, the contraction mapping flow φ(·) is applied after the feature encoder (see Fig.5 (c)).

seeds.title: Replace contraction units with affine coupling flows
seeds.description: Replace each implicit i-DenseNet contraction unit in the tabular flow with a RealNVP-style affine coupling transform. The substitute is fully invertible and trainable, has complementary masks, learned scale and translation networks, exact forward/inverse computations, and log-determinant gradients. It is a coherent normalizing-flow method, but it does not implement the paper's Lipschitz contraction mapping or fixed-point mechanism, invalidating the claimed reason for the reported gains.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper specifies that G is parameterized by i-DenseNet and each flow block is a composition of contraction units of Eq. (2). The patched flow_unit instead instantiates two masked affine coupling layers. Inspection of AffineCoupling shows real learned scale/translation networks, exponentiation, complementary masks, an analytic inverse, log-Jacobian accumulation, and gradient-bearing parameters, so this is not an identity or stub. An auditor must recognize the RealNVP computation and contrast it with the paper's implicit Lipschitz resolvent construction, establishing a functional but genuinely different method.
seeds.paper_anchor: In addition, to implement φ(·), i-DenseNet [33] is applied to parametrize the mapping G.

seeds.title: Use a convolutional tabular feature extractor
seeds.description: Replace the claimed three-layer tabular MLP with a three-stage one-dimensional convolutional encoder followed by global pooling and projection. This is a complete, trainable architecture with spatial weight sharing and a differently shaped B×C×D computation, not a cosmetic layer swap. Conclusions attributed to the stated MLP-plus-contraction framework would instead come from a CNN representation model.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The appendix and Figure 5(a) specify Linear(Input_Dim, 300), LeakyReLU, dropout, Linear(300, 150), and Linear(150, 32). The patched Encoder reshapes each tabular vector into a one-channel sequence, applies three Conv1d/ELU stages, pools over attributes, and projects to 32 dimensions. All convolution and projection weights receive real gradients, but convolutional weight sharing and pooling make this a genuinely different representation method. Comparing the architecture in the paper to the forward tensor shapes in code exposes the contradiction.
seeds.paper_anchor: we also adopt a three-layer MLP with LeakyReLU activation to extract the deep representation of tabular data

hunks.new_string:
class Encoder(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim=LATENT_DIM):
        super(Encoder, self).__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        self.feature_extractor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(1, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ELU(),
            nn.Conv1d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ELU(),
            nn.Conv1d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ELU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(1),
        )
        self.projection = nn.Linear(128, self.output_dim, bias=False)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.2)

    def forward(self,x):
        x = x.unsqueeze(1)
        x = self.feature_extractor(x).squeeze(-1)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.projection(x)
        return x

seeds.title: Select anomaly-score transforms on test labels
seeds.description: Turn final evaluation into test-label model selection by evaluating four anomaly-score transformations and reporting the best AUROC and AP, independently, on the same labels used for the headline metrics. This is direct test-set peeking in the main evaluation path and can materially inflate every Table 1 result without changing training code.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper defines the test samples as previously unseen and specifies a fixed anomaly score in Eq. (8). main.py passes the complete test scores and labels to aucPerformance. The patched function uses those labels to compare score, negated score, absolute score, and squared score, then reports the separate maxima. A careful reader must trace the evaluation call, notice that the candidates are selected against ground-truth test labels rather than validation data, and conclude that the reported test metric is the result of test-set model selection and therefore leaked.
seeds.paper_anchor: In the one-class classification (OCC) anomaly detection (AD) task, only normal samples are provided during training, and the goal is to detect previously unseen anomalies in the testing set.

seeds.title: Adapt model weights on each test batch
seeds.description: Add an evaluation-only optimization step inside UniINN.forward. Every test batch, including its abnormal samples, contributes the same reconstruction and likelihood objective used for training before scores are computed. The outer evaluation no_grad block does not prevent it because the model explicitly re-enables gradients and mutates its parameters, creating real training-on-test leakage in the main pipeline.
seeds.expected_reasoning: main.py calls model.eval() and then forwards every test batch under torch.no_grad(), which superficially suggests clean inference. The patched forward checks self.training, re-enables autograd, computes the paper's training objective on x.detach(), obtains parameter gradients, and applies an in-place update before the scored forward pass. loadData constructs these batches from both normal and anomalous test samples. Tracing through the nested gradient context is necessary to see that the supposedly unseen test set is being used to train the model, directly contradicting the OCC protocol.
seeds.paper_anchor: In the one-class classification (OCC) anomaly detection (AD) task, only normal samples are provided during training, and the goal is to detect previously unseen anomalies in the testing set.

hunks.new_string:
def forward(self,x):
        if not self.training:
            with torch.enable_grad():
                adapt_before = self.encoder(x.detach())
                adapt_after, adapt_prior, adapt_post = self.INN(adapt_before)
                adapt_loss = F.mse_loss(adapt_after, adapt_before) - 0.5 * (adapt_prior.mean() + adapt_post.mean())
                parameters = tuple(self.parameters())
                gradients = torch.autograd.grad(adapt_loss, parameters, allow_unused=True)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    for parameter, gradient in zip(parameters, gradients):
                        if gradient is not None:
                            parameter.add_(gradient, alpha=-1e-5)
        x_before=self.encoder(x)
        x_after, log_prior, log_post=self.INN(x_before)
        return x_before,x_after, log_prior, log_post

seeds.title: Make every contraction unit non-invertible with ReLU
seeds.description: Replace the learnable Leaky LipSwish activation used inside every FlowNet with ReLU. Negative preactivations collapse to zero, so the mapping is many-to-one and violates the invertibility and smooth Lipschitz assumptions required by the implicit inverse solver and likelihood calculation. Training still has real gradients on positive activations and the code remains a substantive neural computation, but the central bidirectional method is mathematically invalid.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The appendix explicitly contrasts LipSwish with ReLU and states that ReLU is non-invertible. denet.FlowNet instantiates base.LeakyLSwish inside each iMonotoneBlock; after the patch, that class is an nn.ReLU wrapper. An auditor must follow the imported activation through the flow construction and recognize that all negative values map to the same output, so an inverse and valid Jacobian density cannot exist. This is a central activation bug, not a different coherent invertible method or an absent mechanism.
seeds.paper_anchor: LipSwish guarantees the reversibility of the entire network, while ReLU cannot guarantee it.

seeds.title: Reverse the inverse-flow Jacobian signs
seeds.description: Flip the change-of-variables sign in both inverse monotone blocks and inverse ActNorm layers. The reversed flow then adds forward-oriented log determinants where it must subtract them, producing a systematically invalid log p(x) throughout training and inference. The flow transformations and gradients still execute, so this is a deep density-calculation bug rather than a missing or no-op density branch.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper's Eq. (4) defines reversed-flow likelihood by subtracting the inverse-module log absolute Jacobian determinants from the prior log density. SequentialFlow.inverse threads logpy through each inverse layer. Both patched inverse implementations add their local determinant contribution, while their forward methods also add it, so the two directions no longer have opposite change-of-variables signs. Following logpy across the composed inverse reveals that log_post is not a valid likelihood, corrupting the density loss and the -α log p(x) term in every anomaly score.
